State the stage range a rating may be applied over

Source: R/fit_rating.R
set_operational_limits.Rd

A rating made by fit_rating() is applied only within the stage range it was gauged over, until the range it may be used over is stated here. That range is a decision, not a property of the data: it might be the gauged range, a structure's limit, a hydraulic argument for extrapolating to a stated stage, or a review outcome. Saying it, and saying why, is what makes a wider application defensible.

The rating is returned as a new version. Its earlier state is kept in rating_history(), and its lifecycle goes back to "draft", since a change to where a rating may be used is a change a reviewer should see. Stages outside the limits are refused by apply_rating(); stages inside them but beyond the gauged range are computed and flagged extrapolated.

Usage

set_operational_limits(x, lower_stage_m, upper_stage_m, basis = NA_character_)

Arguments

x

A FlodeRating or FlodeSegmentedRating.

lower_stage_m, upper_stage_m

The stage range in metres, lower below upper.

basis

Character. Why this range.

Value

A copy of x with the limits in its provenance.

See also

fit_rating(), rating_provenance(), rating_history()

Examples

set.seed(2)
stage_m <- seq(0.5, 3, length.out = 15)
fit <- fit_rating(
  data.frame(stage_m = stage_m, discharge_cms = 3 * stage_m^1.6 * exp(rnorm(15, sd = 0.03))),
  quiet = TRUE
)
limited <- set_operational_limits(fit, 0.4, 3.2, basis = "gauged range plus 0.2 m of judgement")
rating_provenance(limited)$operational_limits
#> $lower_stage_m
#> [1] 0.4
#> 
#> $upper_stage_m
#> [1] 3.2
#> 
#> $basis
#> [1] "gauged range plus 0.2 m of judgement"
#> 
rating_history(limited)[, .(class, lifecycle, note)]
#>          class lifecycle
#>         <char>    <char>
#> 1: FlodeRating     draft
#> 2: FlodeRating     draft
#>                                                                             note
#>                                                                           <char>
#> 1:                                                                          <NA>
#> 2: operational limits set to 0.4 to 3.2 m (gauged range plus 0.2 m of judgement)
